> and the **answers** to the "👉 Your turn" tasks are on the course website.

**The question:** the volcano told us *which* genes changed. A **heatmap** shows their
*pattern* — every top gene across every sample, in one picture.

## Setup {-}

```{r setup07, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- c("data", "../data", "project/data", "../project/data")
data_dir <- data_dir[dir.exists(data_dir)][1]
counts <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "gene_counts.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
meta   <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.tsv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
de     <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "DE_biofilm_vs_planktonic_24h.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

We'll use the **`pheatmap`** package — a dedicated heatmap tool that clusters the genes
and samples for you and adds colour bars for the sample groups.

Pick the genes that changed most, pull their expression into a matrix, and label the
samples:

```{r}
top_genes <- de %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  slice_max(abs(log2FoldChange), n = 25) %>%
  pull(gene_id)

mat <- counts %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% top_genes) %>%
  select(-gene_name) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene_id") %>%
  as.matrix()
logmat <- log2(mat + 1)

# label each sample (column) with its lifestyle and timepoint
annotation <- meta %>%
  select(sample, lifestyle, timepoint) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample")
```

Now a single call draws it — clustered, row-scaled and annotated:

```{r, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(pheatmap)

pheatmap(
  logmat,
  scale          = "row",        # z-score each gene, so we compare patterns not levels
  annotation_col = annotation,   # colour bars for lifestyle & timepoint
  show_colnames  = FALSE,
  fontsize_row   = 7,
  main           = "Top genes: biofilm vs planktonic (row-scaled)"
)
```

The clustering pulls the biofilm and planktonic samples into separate blocks, and the
colour bars at the top confirm it — the same story as the volcano, now gene by gene.

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Principle:</strong> a heatmap shows a whole matrix at once by mapping each
  value to a colour. <code>pheatmap</code> adds the clustering (dendrograms) and the
  annotation bars that turn a wall of colour into a readable story. Row-scaling (z-score)
  lets genes on very different scales share one colour key.
</div>

<div class="tip">
  <strong>💡 Tip:</strong> the colour bars come straight from your <code>annotation</code>
  table — add more metadata columns to it and <code>pheatmap</code> will show them too.
</div>
